ev.q: Significant state and regional variation in MCC prevalence was found
One in four (25.7%) U.S. adults had a diagnosis of MCC
Prevalence estimates of MCC were higher than the national average in 10 states
only the Pacific region prevalence was consistently lower than the national average when stratified by age
Data from the 2014 National Health Interview Survey (NHIS) were used to estimate prevalence

methods_quotes.q: For all estimates, sampling weights were used; analyses were conducted using SUDAAN 11.0 software to account for the complex sample design.
Two-tailed significance tests comparing state and regional prevalence to national prevalence were adjusted to account for dependent samples using procedures described elsewhere
All presented differences were found to be significant using two-tailed significance tests (p<0.05).
Taylor series linearization was used for estimation of standard errors for the 10 U.S. states with the largest sample sizes
The 95% confidence intervals for each state were derived by multiplying this standard error with 1.96
National Center for Health Statistics standard for reliability is that an estimate have a relative standard error <30.0%
